You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Clearing the combobox never calls onChange(null), so the selection can't be cleared.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Combobox Enter throws after `options` shrinks while an option is active. `src/Combobox.tsx:81` does `options[activeIndex].value` with a stale index. Probe: open, `{ArrowDown}` x3 on 3 options, rerender with 1 option, `{Enter}`. Result: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'value')` as an unhandled error, and onChange is never called.
- [blocking] Combobox `aria-activedescendant` dangles after the same change (checklist: every aria-* id reference must resolve). Probe: same steps, then `input.getAttribute("aria-activedescendant")` gives `«rk»-option-2`, which is not in the DOM.
- [blocking] Dialog focus escapes via Tab when the parent ignores onOpenChange and the user clicks the backdrop (D3 "focus never reaches elements outside via Tab"). The backdrop mousedown moves focus to body, so the Tab keydown never reaches the dialog's `keepTabWithin` handler (`src/Dialog.tsx:69`). Probe: `<button>outside-before</button>` then `<Dialog open onOpenChange={()=>{}}>`, `user.click(dialog.parentElement)`, `user.tab()`. Activeelement after Tab is `<button>outside-before</button>`.
- [blocking] Controlled Tabs fires onValueChange twice for one click when the parent ignores the update. The focus handler (`src/Tabs.tsx:141`) and the click handler (`:135`) both call `select` with the same stale `selected`. Probe: `<Tabs value="a" onValueChange={spy}>`, `user.click(tab B)`, `expect(spy.mock.calls.length).toBe(1)` fails with `expected 2 to be 1`. Uncontrolled mode gives 1 call, and a parent that updates `value` also gives 1 call.
- [minor] Tabbing into a tablist whose value matches no tab (`value="nope"`) calls onValueChange("a") without any user selection, because focus selects (`src/Tabs.tsx:141`). This is arguably what "selection follows focus" means, but it is a side effect a parent may not expect. Reproduced: `spy` called once on `user.tab()`.
- [minor] Hidden Tab that is the selected value (disabled and selected) gets tabIndex 0 (`tabStop` uses `selected` even when disabled). Not reproduced as a bug; noted from reading.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog focus escapes when the focused element unmounts. Focus goes to BODY, and keydown on body never reaches the dialog's `handleKeyDown`, so `keepTabWithin` never runs. Reproduced: a button inside the dialog removes itself on click, then `await user.tab()` lands on `outside BUTTON`. Expected focus to stay inside the dialog. Fix idea: handle Tab/Escape at document level while open, or refocus the dialog when focus leaves it.
- [blocking] Nested dialogs that mount open together end with focus in the outer dialog. The outer effect runs after the inner one and steals focus to `o1`. Reproduced: `render(<Dialog open title="Outer"><button>o1</button><Dialog open title="Inner"><button>i1</button></Dialog></Dialog>)` gives `document.activeElement` = `o1`, so Escape and Tab act on the outer dialog. Only the case where the inner opens later was tested.
- [minor] Combobox option ids depend on `useId` and are unique, but a stale `activeIndex` can reappear as active if the option list changes so that the same index becomes visible again. Not reproduced.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix the reproduced bugs below in an already-built accessible React 19 component library at /tmp/ff-eval-3nnaqpes/workspace (uncommitted work: src/Tabs.tsx, src/Dialog.tsx, src/Combobox.tsx, src/index.ts, README.md, tests/*.test.tsx; 84 tests pass now). For each fix, write a failing test first in the matching tests/<Component>.test.tsx, then make it pass.

FIXES:
1. Combobox stale active option (C4/C5): open, ArrowDown x3 on 3 options, rerender with 1 option, then Enter throws (`options[activeIndex]` is undefined), and aria-activedescendant points at a missing id. Derive the effective active index during render: it counts only if it is in `visible` and not disabled, otherwise null. Use that value for aria-activedescendant, Enter and arrow stepping. Test the shrink case and the case where the active option becomes disabled.
2. Dialog focus escape (D3): with the parent ignoring onOpenChange, clicking the backdrop moves focus to body, and Tab then reaches outside elements. Fix: in the backdrop mousedown handler, when target === currentTarget, call event.preventDefault() so focus stays put. Test: render a button outside, then a Dialog with a no-op onOpenChange. Click the backdrop (the dialog's parentElement), press Tab, and assert that focus is inside the dialog.
3. Nested dialogs: React synthetic events bubble through portals, so the keydowns of a Dialog rendered inside another Dialog's children reach the outer DialogSurface's handleKeyDown. Escape closes both, and the outer keepTabWithin steals focus from the inner dialog. Fix: in handleKeyDown, return early unless `dialogRef.current?.contains(event.target as Node)`. Test: an outer Dialog whose children include an open inner Dialog with two buttons. Escape calls only the inner onOpenChange. Tab and Shift+Tab inside the inner dialog keep focus inside it.
4. Tabs double onValueChange (T5/T6): in a controlled Tabs whose parent ignores updates, one click fires onValueChange twice (onFocus, then onClick). Fix: drop the selection in onFocus. Select from handleKeyDown after `target.focus()` (select the target tab's value, read from a data attribute or by looking it up) and from click. Test: controlled, ignoring parent, click → exactly 1 call; tabbing into a tablist with value="nope" → 0 calls and focus lands on the first enabled tab; arrows/Home/End still select in both modes. Keep the README accurate.
5. Combobox: give the `<label>` an id and set `aria-labelledby` on the listbox to it (APG). Add a test.

Also, if it's quick, remove the "not wrapped in act(...)" warnings that the Tabs tests print, which come from calling element.focus() outside act (use `act(() => el.focus())` or user-event).

CONSTRAINTS: No new deps; don't edit package.json/tsconfig/vitest config. Keep all existing tests passing; change an existing test only if it asserted the old onFocus-selection behavior, and say which.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Tabs
- T1 `<Tabs defaultValue? value? onValueChange?>` wraps `<TabList aria-label>`, `<Tab value disabled?>`, `<TabPanel value>`. TabList has role="tablist" and the given aria-label; Tab is a `<button type="button" role="tab">` with aria-selected="true|false" and aria-controls = its panel's id; TabPanel has role="tabpanel", aria-labelledby = its tab's id, tabIndex=0, and the `hidden` attribute when not selected (only the selected panel is visible). Ids derive from one useId per Tabs plus the value, so two Tabs instances on a page never share ids.
- T2 Roving tabindex: the selected tab has tabIndex=0, every other tab tabIndex=-1. If no tab matches the current value (e.g. value="nope"), the first enabled tab gets tabIndex=0 so the tablist stays keyboard-reachable.
- T3 ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move focus to the next/previous enabled tab, wrapping last→first and first→last, skipping disabled tabs; Home/End go to the first/last enabled tab. These keys call preventDefault. Selection follows focus: moving focus selects that tab (calls onValueChange(value), and in uncontrolled mode shows its panel).
- T4 Clicking an enabled tab selects it. A disabled tab has aria-disabled="true"; clicking it does nothing and keyboard nav skips it.
- T5 Uncontrolled: `defaultValue` sets the initial tab; with neither value nor defaultValue, the first enabled tab is selected. Controlled: `value` wins; onValueChange is called with the new value; if the parent doesn't update `value`, the selected tab and visible panel don't change.
- T6 Hostile: all tabs disabled → arrow/Home/End do nothing and nothing throws; a single tab → ArrowRight keeps focus on it without calling onValueChange with a different value; Tabs whose tabs are rendered conditionally/reordered still navigate in DOM order (derive order from the DOM `[role=tab]` elements inside the tablist at keydown time, not from registration order); onValueChange is not called when re-selecting the already-selected tab.
Dialog
- D1 `<Dialog open onOpenChange title description?>children</Dialog>`. When open is false nothing is rendered. When open is true it renders via createPortal into document.body: a backdrop element containing an element with role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby → the title element (an h2) and, only when `description` is given, aria-describedby → the description element (a p). With no description there is no aria-describedby attribute.
- D2 On open, focus moves to the first focusable element inside the dialog (buttons, links with href, inputs/selects/textareas not disabled, [tabindex] not "-1", contenteditable); if there is none, the dialog element itself (tabIndex=-1) receives focus.
- D3 Focus trap: Tab on the last focusable wraps to the first; Shift+Tab on the first wraps to the last; with no focusables, Tab/Shift+Tab keep focus on the dialog. Focus never reaches elements outside the dialog via Tab.
- D4 Escape calls onOpenChange(false) — unless the keydown's defaultPrevented is already true (so a child widget that consumed Escape, like an open Combobox, doesn't also close the dialog). Clicking the backdrop calls onOpenChange(false); clicking inside the dialog does not; a press that starts inside the dialog and ends on the backdrop (mousedown inside, mouseup/click on backdrop) does not close it.
- D5 When the dialog closes (open → false) or unmounts, focus returns to the element that had focus right before it opened. If that element was removed from the document, nothing throws. This works under `<React.StrictMode>` (double-run effects must not record an element inside the dialog as the "previous" focus).
- D6 It's controlled: if the parent ignores onOpenChange(false), the dialog stays open.
Combobox
- C1 `<Combobox label options value onChange placeholder?>`; options are `{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }`, value is `string | null`, onChange(value: string | null). Renders a `<label>` (htmlFor the input) with the label text, an `<input role="combobox" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-expanded aria-controls={listboxId}>`, and a `<ul role="listbox">` (always in the DOM so aria-controls resolves; `hidden` when closed) with `<li role="option" id>` children. Options have aria-selected="true" only for the option whose value === `value`, "false" otherwise; disabled options have aria-disabled="true". placeholder is passed to the input.
- C2 The input shows the label of the option matching `value` (empty string if value is null or matches nothing), and updates when `value` changes from outside.
- C3 Typing opens the listbox and filters options whose label contains the typed text, case-insensitively (substring match; "AN" matches "Banana"). Opening via ArrowDown/ArrowUp without typing shows all options (even when the input currently shows the selected label). Typed text containing regex characters like "(" or "." is treated literally and doesn't throw.
- C4 ArrowDown/ArrowUp: when closed, open the listbox and make the first/last enabled option active; when open, move the active option to the next/previous enabled option, wrapping, skipping disabled ones. The active option is exposed via aria-activedescendant on the input (and nothing else is focused — focus stays on the input). When no option is active, aria-activedescendant is absent. After the text changes, no option is active until an arrow key is pressed. If every visible option is disabled, arrows leave nothing active and nothing throws. Arrow keys call preventDefault.
- C5 Enter with an active option calls onChange(option.value), closes the listbox and sets the input text to that label. Enter when the listbox is closed or with no active option does not call onChange and does not preventDefault when closed (so a surrounding form can submit). Clicking an enabled option selects it the same way (use mousedown preventDefault so the input keeps focus); clicking a disabled option does nothing and keeps the listbox open.
- C6 Escape while open closes the listbox without calling onChange, restores the input text to the current value's label, calls preventDefault and stopPropagation on the event. Escape while closed does nothing (does not preventDefault). Tab/blur closes the listbox without selecting and restores the text to the current value's label (without preventing Tab's default).
- C7 When the listbox is open and no options match, a "No results" message is shown (an element with role="status" containing exactly "No results"), and the listbox has no options. The message is not shown when closed or when there are matches. Empty `options` array + ArrowDown → "No results", nothing throws.
- C8 Clearing the input text entirely (user deletes all text) calls onChange(null). Controlled: if the parent doesn't update `value` after onChange, the input text reverts to the label of `value` once the listbox closes.
- C9 Two Comboboxes on one page have distinct input/listbox/option ids.
Integration
- I1 A Combobox inside an open Dialog: Escape with the listbox open closes only the listbox (onOpenChange not called); a second Escape closes the dialog.
Package
- P1 `src/index.ts` exports Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel, Dialog, Combobox and their prop types; no CSS anywhere.
- P2 README.md documents each component: a short usage example, a props table (name, type, required/default, description) and a keyboard table, matching the implementation.
- P3 `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` both pass; tests cover every criterion above.

CHECKS: while working `pnpm vitest run tests/<File>.test.tsx`; at the end `pnpm test` then `pnpm typecheck`.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 2 (sent after review 2) ===
GOAL: Fix two reproduced Dialog focus bugs in /tmp/ff-eval-3nnaqpes/workspace/src/Dialog.tsx (an accessible React 19 component library; all work uncommitted; 93 tests pass). Write the failing tests first in tests/Dialog.test.tsx.

BUGS:
1. Focus escapes when the focused element inside the dialog unmounts. Focus falls to <body>, and keydown on body never reaches the dialog's React onKeyDown, so Tab reaches outside elements and Escape does nothing. Repro: a button inside the dialog that removes itself on click; after clicking it, `await user.tab()` lands on an outside button. Expected: Tab moves focus into the dialog (first focusable), and Escape still calls onOpenChange(false).
2. Nested dialogs that mount open in the same render (`<Dialog open title="Outer"><button>o1</button><Dialog open title="Inner"><button>i1</button></Dialog></Dialog>`) end with focus on o1, because the outer's effect runs after the inner's and steals focus. Expected: focus on i1. Escape calls only the inner onOpenChange, and Tab stays inside the inner dialog.

DESIGN (follow unless you find a concrete problem with it):
- Keep a module-level stack `openDialogs: HTMLElement[]` of open dialog elements.
- Capture the "previous focus" during the first render with `useState(() => document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null)`, not in the effect. Render runs before any child effect, so both nested dialogs record the real opener, and it is StrictMode-safe.
- In the mount effect: if document.activeElement is already inside another dialog on the stack (a nested child that mounted first), insert this dialog just below that one in the stack and don't move focus. Otherwise push it and focus its first focusable element (or the dialog itself).
- In the effect cleanup: remove the dialog from the stack. Then restore focus: if `previous` is connected and either the stack is empty or `previous` is inside the top dialog, focus `previous`. Otherwise, if the stack isn't empty, focus the top dialog's first focusable element (or that dialog itself). Never throw.
- Move the Tab/Escape handling from React onKeyDown to a native `document` keydown listener that the effect adds and removes. A dialog handles an event only if it "owns" it: the dialog that contains event.target owns it, and if no open dialog contains the target (e.g. focus on body), the top of the stack owns it. Escape: if `!event.defaultPrevented`, call onOpenChange(false) (read the latest onOpenChange from a ref). Tab: run the existing keepTabWithin logic. When focus is on body/outside, that logic already sends Tab to the first focusable and Shift+Tab to the last. Keep passing the consumer's `onKeyDown` prop through to the dialog element.
- Keep the backdrop mousedown/click behavior as it is.
- Make sure I1 still passes: the Combobox calls preventDefault and stopPropagation on Escape when its listbox is open, so the dialog must not close. Both the defaultPrevented check and the stopped propagation guard this.

Keep the existing nested-dialog, StrictMode, backdrop and focus-restore tests passing unchanged.
